original_question: For dimension d >= 2 and a nonzero direction l in R^d, find conditions that imply a zero-one law for directional transience, namely that P_0[A_l] is always either 0 or 1, where A_l is the event that X_n · l tends to infinity. In particular, are the assumptions of i.i.d. cookie stacks, a deterministic bound on the number of non-placebo cookies per site, and uniform ellipticity sufficient?
target_in_paper: Problem 3.20 (Section 3.2): for excited random walk on Z^d with d ≥ 2, find conditions implying the directional-transience zero-one law P_0[A_ℓ] ∈ {0,1} for every nonzero direction ℓ, and in particular ask whether (IID), (BD), and (UEL) are sufficient.
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the correct open problem in the paper: it is about dimensions d ≥ 2, the event A_ℓ of transience in a fixed nonzero direction ℓ, the zero-one question P_0[A_ℓ] ∈ {0,1}, and it explicitly singles out the candidate assumptions (IID), (BD), and (UEL), exactly as Problem 3.20 does.
missing_details: The ambient model should be stated explicitly: a nearest-neighbor excited random walk X=(X_n)_{n≥0} on Z^d with underlying simple symmetric random walk and cookie environment law P on Ω.
The probability in the question is the averaged law P_0 for a walk started at 0, not a quenched law P_{0,ω}.
The paper asks for a condition that yields the zero-one law for all directions ℓ ∈ R^d with ℓ ≠ 0, not merely for one fixed direction.
A_ℓ should be defined exactly as A_ℓ = {lim_{n→∞} X_n·ℓ = ∞}.
The hypothesis (IID) should be spelled out as: the family of cookie stacks (ω(z,·,·))_{z∈Z^d} is i.i.d. under P.
The hypothesis (UEL) should be defined exactly as: there exists κ>0 such that P-a.s. ω(z,e,i) ≥ κ for all z∈Z^d, e in the set E of unit coordinate vectors, and i∈N.
The hypothesis (BD) should be defined via M(z) = inf{j ∈ N_0 : for all e∈E and all i>j, ω(z,e,i)=1/(2d)}, together with the existence of a deterministic M<∞ such that P-a.s. M(z)≤M for all z∈Z^d.
To be paper-faithful, the question should acknowledge the nearby weaker proved result: Theorem 3.16 gives only P_0[A_ℓ ∪ A_{-ℓ}] = P_0[|X_n·ℓ|→∞] ∈ {0,1}, not the desired zero-one law for A_ℓ alone.
The reason the paper highlights (IID), (BD), and (UEL) is the one-dimensional analogue: Theorem 3.10 gives the corresponding 0-1 law in d=1 under (IID), (BD), and (WEL).
The nearby context also records a separate sufficient condition for P_0[A_ℓ]=1, namely (IID), (UEL), (POSℓ), and δ·ℓ>0 in Theorem 3.19; this helps delimit the exact gap that Problem 3.20 asks about.
refined_question: Let X=(X_n)_{n≥0} be a nearest-neighbor excited random walk on Z^d, d≥2, started at 0 under the averaged law P_0 associated with a cookie-environment law P on Ω, and for each nonzero direction ℓ∈R^d define A_ℓ := {lim_{n→∞} X_n·ℓ = ∞}. Find assumptions on P that imply the directional-transience zero-one law P_0[A_ℓ] ∈ {0,1} for every ℓ∈R^d with ℓ≠0. In particular, is this zero-one law already implied by (IID), meaning that the cookie stacks (ω(z,·,·))_{z∈Z^d} are i.i.d. under P; (BD), meaning that there exists a deterministic M<∞ such that P-a.s. M(z)≤M for all z, where M(z)=inf{j∈N_0: ω(z,e,i)=1/(2d) for all e∈E and all i>j}; and (UEL), meaning that there exists κ>0 such that P-a.s. ω(z,e,i)≥κ for all z∈Z^d, e∈E, and i∈N?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 3.20 in Section 3.2 almost verbatim: that problem asks for conditions implying P_0[A_ℓ]∈{0,1} for all nonzero directions ℓ in dimensions d≥2, and then explicitly asks whether (IID), (BD), and (UEL) are sufficient. Definition 3.1 supplies the exact event A_ℓ. The nearby context shows why this is the right sharpening: Theorem 3.16 proves only the weaker zero-one law for A_ℓ∪ A_{-ℓ}, Theorem 3.19 proves P_0[A_ℓ]=1 under additional positivity assumptions, and Problem 3.5 together with Theorem 3.10 gives the one-dimensional analogue that motivates the candidate hypothesis (IID)+(BD)+(UEL). So the refined question should remain narrowly focused on the multidimensional zero-one law for A_ℓ itself, not on broader recurrence/transience questions.
